cases.query: We have a long list of nice-to-have improvements, but I need to know what is actually committed and when this work will stop.
Please turn the accepted concerns into a bounded plan; I do not want adjacent opportunities to keep moving the finish line.
The request says make the dashboard better. I need to turn that into something we can verify and state what is out of scope.
Before planning, check that our restatement of the user's problem is faithful; there are two plausible interpretations.
We are about to make a risky storage migration. What checks should exist in the plan so we can know it worked?
This is a one-line copy change, but the team is proposing a full browser matrix and load test. Decide how much verification is proportionate.
Both approaches work, but one introduces a cache and an extra service layer. Decide whether the current task really needs that.
I am about to add a date formatter; first check whether the repo already has one under our current constraints.
I keep following references into more files, but I cannot name the decision each file will change.
A permission rule must stay identical in the HTTP layer and the background worker. Decide where that rule belongs.
The handler and the domain service could both validate this invariant. Which boundary should own the check?
One small implementation detail is uncertain, but it is reversible and cannot change public behavior. I need to proceed without turning it into a requirement.
The new retry path catches a timeout and returns stale cache data. Make sure the caller's success contract is still true.
While implementing, we discovered that the API response has a new required field. That changes the accepted scope; should the old plan continue?
Before commit, remove code and abstractions this change does not need, even if they look useful later.
A review comment says the migration is unsafe. Check the claim against the code and tests before changing anything.
The test result was captured before a generated file changed; record exactly which artifact revision the evidence covers.
All automated checks pass, but one acceptance path was never exercised. Either add evidence or call the gap out explicitly.
Map each acceptance criterion to its test or manual observation so the final report shows what is covered.
I only ran unit tests and typecheck. Can I tell the user the feature is deployed and accepted?
We are handing off with a known migration limitation and one failed optional check. Decide what the next engineer must know.
The context was compacted and I only have a summary. I am about to edit; how should I recover the real request and current file state?
Another agent reported success and supplied a diff. Before I continue, verify that its summary matches the actual commit and test output.
We are pausing for a week. Write a note that preserves the decisions and current state without including exploratory dead ends.
The user rejected the direction I started. Stop building on it and return to the last authoritative baseline before continuing.
Write tests from the acceptance criteria, not from the helper functions I happened to create.
This test reaches into private state and asserts an implementation detail. Rewrite it around behavior callers can observe.
The test failed after my change. Decide whether the expected behavior or the production code is wrong before editing the test.
Is this rare edge case worth a permanent regression test, or is the protection disproportionate?
I am opening a PR that fixes a React cache bug; a reviewer will see it without our chat history, so make the context and decision self-contained.
The branch now contains a bug fix and a broad refactor. Prepare it for review without mixing two scopes.
This change alters a Knowledge Pack benchmark contract and touches the schema. What review and validation gate must be completed before implementation?
Review is in progress and I have fixes for a dependency upgrade that broke React hooks. Should I amend the reviewed commit or add new commits?
AI helped draft this PR and suggested issues that I resolved. What must the pull request disclose?
This issue mixes a runner bug, a schema change, and a docs cleanup. Reshape it so each reviewable problem has testable acceptance criteria.
After editing the Pack release issue on GitHub, check that the actual saved Markdown did not flatten the lists or lose paragraph breaks.
The Practice trigger uses topic words like schema and matches validation requests even when the action is about release provenance. Rewrite the applicability condition.
One Practice draft tells authors how to choose a file format and how to verify release installation; these are separate decisions.
Two Practices both answer how should I name this Pack, and users cannot tell which action applies. Decide how to separate their triggers or merge them.
I need a retrieval test set with a direct prompt, a paraphrase, a query aimed at the neighboring Practice, and a near miss that should not select it.
YAML validation passed and every React example file is present; can I say the Pack's guidance is semantically validated?
A component stores fullName in state and recomputes it whenever firstName changes. Simplify it using the current props.
When the cart count is zero, the conditional block renders the number 0 on the page.
服务端输出的时间和客户端首次渲染的时间不同，页面因此出现 hydration 警告。应该如何处理这个差异？
两个子组件各自保存筛选条件，再通过回调互相同步，经常不一致。应该怎么组织这个状态？
A dialog receives isCreating and isEditing booleans, and both can be true. Model the mutually exclusive modes so invalid combinations cannot be passed.
An editable threshold should follow the server's changing default until the user explicitly saves their own value.
useState creates a large parsed dataset on every render even though only the first value is used.
A timer identifier is stored in state even though changing it never affects rendering.
A useCallback uses setItems(prev => ...) and omits items from dependencies, but the callback also reads an unrelated reactive filter.
